headline.hi: Do important theorems jo har saal exam mein aate hain!
headline.en: Two important theorems that appear every year in exams!

subtext.hi: Is lesson mein hum do sabse important theorems seekhenge — Theorem 10.1 (Tangent perpendicular to Radius) aur Theorem 10.2 (Equal Tangents from External Point).
subtext.en: In this lesson, we learn the two most important theorems — Theorem 10.1 (Tangent perpendicular to Radius) and Theorem 10.2 (Equal Tangents from External Point).

text.hi: Is lesson mein hum do sabse important theorems seekhenge — Theorem 10.1 (Tangent perpendicular to Radius) aur Theorem 10.2 (Equal Tangents from External Point). Inke proofs aur applications dono aane chahiye!
text.en: In this lesson, we learn the two most important theorems — Theorem 10.1 (Tangent perpendicular to Radius) and Theorem 10.2 (Equal Tangents from External Point). Both proofs and applications are required!

content.hi:
Statement: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
📝 Given: Circle with centre O, tangent XY at point P
📝 To Prove: OP ⊥ XY (matlab OP radius tangent ke perpendicular hai)
Proof by Contradiction:
Step 1: Maan lo OP ⊥ XY nahi hai
Step 2: Toh koi aur point Q hoga XY pe jisse OQ ⊥ XY ho
Step 3: Right triangle OQP mein, OQ < OP (hypotenuse sabse badi)
Step 4: Lekin Q circle ke andar hai (kyunki OQ < radius OP)
Step 5: Iska matlab XY circle ko do points pe kaat rahi hai — contradiction!
Step 6: Isliye OP ⊥ XY hi hona chahiye ✅
content.en:
Statement: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
📝 Given: Circle with centre O, tangent XY at point P
📝 To Prove: OP ⊥ XY (meaning OP is perpendicular to the tangent)
Proof by Contradiction:
Step 1: Assume OP is NOT perpendicular to XY
Step 2: Then some other point Q on XY has OQ ⊥ XY
Step 3: In right triangle OQP, OQ < OP (hypotenuse is longest)
Step 4: But Q lies inside the circle (since OQ < radius OP)
Step 5: This means XY cuts the circle at two points — contradiction!
Step 6: Therefore OP ⊥ XY ✅

content.hi: Proof by Contradiction: Assume opposite → Show contradiction → Original statement true
content.en: Proof by Contradiction: Assume opposite → Show contradiction → Original statement true

content.hi: Theorem 10.1 ka Use: Yeh theorem har tangent problem mein kaam aata hai. Jab bhi tangent mile, right triangle banao aur Pythagoras lagao.
content.en: Use of Theorem 10.1: This theorem is used in every tangent problem. Whenever you see a tangent, form a right triangle and apply Pythagoras.

explanation.content:
If XY is tangent at P, then OP ⊥ XY
So, ∠OPX = ∠OPY = 90°

content.hi: Example: Radius = 5cm, Tangent length = 12cm → Distance from centre = √(5²+12²) = 13cm
content.en: Example: Radius = 5cm, Tangent length = 12cm → Distance from centre = √(5²+12²) = 13cm

content.hi:
Statement: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
📝 Given: Circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PA and PB
📝 To Prove: PA = PB
Proof:
Step 1: Join OP, OA, OB
Step 2: ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Theorem 10.1)
Step 3: OA = OB (radii of same circle)
Step 4: OP = OP (common side)
Step 5: ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP (RHS congruence rule)
Step 6: Therefore, PA = PB (CPCT) ✅
Bonus: ∠AOP = ∠BOP aur ∠APO = ∠BPO bhi equal hote hain!
content.en:
Statement: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
📝 Given: Circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PA and PB
📝 To Prove: PA = PB
Proof:
Step 1: Join OP, OA, OB
Step 2: ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Theorem 10.1)
Step 3: OA = OB (radii of same circle)
Step 4: OP = OP (common side)
Step 5: ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP (RHS congruence rule)
Step 6: Therefore, PA = PB (CPCT) ✅
Bonus: ∠AOP = ∠BOP and ∠APO = ∠BPO are also equal!

content.hi: RHS Congruence: Right angle, Hypotenuse common, Side (radius) equal → Triangles congruent → PA = PB
content.en: RHS Congruence: Right angle, Hypotenuse common, Side (radius) equal → Triangles congruent → PA = PB

content.hi: Theorem 10.2 ke Important Results: Jab do tangents ek external point se nikalti hain, toh bahut saari properties ek saath apply hoti hain. In sab ko yaad rakhna zaroori hai.
content.en: Important Results from Theorem 10.2: When two tangents are drawn from an external point, many properties apply simultaneously. Remember all of them.

explanation.content:
PA = PB (Tangent lengths equal)
∠AOP = ∠BOP (OP angle bisector)
∠APO = ∠BPO (OP bisects ∠APB)
OP is perpendicular bisector of AB

content.hi: Example: PA = PB = 12cm, OP = 13cm, OA = 5cm → Sab consistent hai kyunki 5²+12²=13²
content.en: Example: PA = PB = 12cm, OP = 13cm, OA = 5cm → All consistent since 5²+12²=13²

problem.hi: Do tangents PA aur PB ek circle pe point P se milti hain. Agar ∠APB = 70°, toh ∠OAB nikaalo.
problem.en: Two tangents PA and PB meet at point P. If ∠APB = 70°, find ∠OAB.

steps.hi: Step 1: Isosceles triangle properties. Step 2: Tangent ⊥ Radius. Step 3: Angle subtract karo.
steps.en: Step 1: Isosceles triangle properties. Step 2: Tangent ⊥ Radius. Step 3: Subtract angles.

problem.hi: Do tangents PA aur PB circle ke centre O se external point P pe milti hain. Agar ∠AOB = 110°, toh ∠APB nikaalo.
problem.en: Two tangents PA and PB from centre O meet at external point P. If ∠AOB = 110°, find ∠APB.

steps.hi: 🎯 Quadrilateral OAPB mein hamesha ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180° (kyunki do 90° angles hain)!
steps.en: 🎯 In quadrilateral OAPB, always ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180° (since two angles are 90°)!

problem.hi: Ek circle mein tangent PQ point P pe chord PR ko milti hai. Agar ∠QPR = 50°, toh angle jo arc PR centre pe banta hai, nikaalo.
problem.en: In a circle, tangent PQ at point P meets chord PR. If ∠QPR = 50°, find the angle subtended by arc PR at the centre.

steps.hi: Tangent aur chord ke beech ka angle = Us chord ke opposite arc pe banta hua angle
steps.en: Angle between tangent and chord = Angle in alternate segment

steps.hi: So, ∠QPR = ∠PSR (where S is any point on alternate segment)
steps.en: So, ∠QPR = ∠PSR = 50° (where S is any point on alternate segment)

steps.hi: Centre pe angle = 2 × Circumference pe angle
steps.en: Angle at centre = 2 × Angle at circumference

steps.hi: Alternate Segment Theorem: Tangent-Chord angle = Angle in alternate segment
steps.en: Alternate Segment Theorem: Tangent-Chord angle = Angle in alternate segment

question.hi: Theorem 10.1 ke according, tangent radius ke ______ hoti hai.
question.en: According to Theorem 10.1, tangent is ______ to the radius.

explanation.hi: Tangent point of contact pe radius ke perpendicular hoti hai.
explanation.en: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

question.hi: External point P se do tangents PA aur PB hain. Agar PA = 8cm, toh PB = ?
question.en: From external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn. If PA = 8cm, then PB = ?

question.hi: Quadrilateral OAPB mein ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180° hamesha hota hai.
question.en: In quadrilateral OAPB, ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180° always holds true.

explanation.hi: ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°, so bache hue do angles ka sum 180° hona chahiye.
explanation.en: ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°, so the remaining two angles must sum to 180°.

question.hi: ΔOAP aur ΔOBP kaunse congruence rule se congruent hain?
question.en: ΔOAP and ΔOBP are congruent by which rule?

explanation.hi: Right angle, Hypotenuse common (OP), Side equal (OA=OB=radius) → RHS congruence.
explanation.en: Right angle, Hypotenuse common (OP), Side equal (OA=OB=radius) → RHS congruence.

notes.hi: Theorem 10.1: Tangent ⊥ Radius (point of contact pe 90°)
notes.en: Theorem 10.1: Tangent ⊥ Radius (90° at point of contact)

notes.hi: Theorem 10.2: External point se 2 tangents ki lengths equal (PA = PB)
notes.en: Theorem 10.2: Two tangents from external point have equal lengths (PA = PB)

notes.hi: Alternate Segment Theorem: Tangent-chord angle = Angle in alternate segment
notes.en: Alternate Segment Theorem: Tangent-chord angle = Angle in alternate segment

notes.hi: Centre angle = 2 × Circumference angle (same arc ke liye)
notes.en: Centre angle = 2 × Circumference angle (for same arc)

summary.hi: Theorem 10.1 (Tangent ⊥ Radius) aur Theorem 10.2 (External point se equal tangents) — dono theorems ke proofs aur applications ab clear hain.
summary.en: Theorem 10.1 (Tangent ⊥ Radius) and Theorem 10.2 (equal tangents from an external point) — you now understand both proofs and their applications.
